summary: R. Gayathri is an Indology scholar who conducted doctoral studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics, later serving at the New York Herald Tribune, Guaranty Trust Company, and J.P. Morgan & Co.

R. H. Blyth (1898–1964) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of London. He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (~1940–1942), and taught Robert Baker Aitken.

R. H. Tawney (1880–1962) was a historian who studied at Rugby School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1913–1949).

R. K. Bodhe, who works in Indology, studied at the R.C. Patel Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (2017–2019). Bodhe held a post as Research Officer at the Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005).

R. Keller Kimbrough is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who earned a PhD at Yale University and taught Aaron P. Proffitt. Kimbrough held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2013).
R. N. Gadre was an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1958).
R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte and served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).

R. Ramanujachari was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who served as Professor of Philosophy at Annamalai University (attested 1938–1940) and edited the Journal of the Annamalai University (attested 1950).

R. Sathyanarayana (1927–2020) was an Indology scholar who earned a master's at the University of Mysore. He taught at Sarada Vilas College (1949–1984), served as President of the Indian Music Congress, and taught Andrey Klebanov.
R. T. Vyas is an Indology scholar who served as General Editor of Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1988) and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (1993–1994).

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. He held posts at Presidency College Chennai, University of Madras, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and Adyar Library (1994–2000).
R. Venkatraman is an Indology and history scholar who earned a PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, later serving there as Reader (attested 1990).

Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a philosopher who studied at St. Xavier's Collegiate School and University College London. He founded Visva-Bharati University and the Sino-Indian Cultural Society.

Rachael Margaret Griffiths is a scholar in Tibetology and computational fields who completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford in 2020. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2023) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (2024).
Rachael Wiseman is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of York (~2004–2008) and served as a Reader at the University of Liverpool in 2023.

Rachel H. Pang works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia and served as Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College (attested 2019).

Rachel Van Meter Baumer (1928–1995) was an Indologist who studied under Thomas Welbourne Clark and earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (~1959–1964). She held posts at Michigan State, Minnesota, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1969–1978).

Rachelle M. Scott is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed her dissertation at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay. She held a faculty post as Associate Professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (2002; attested 2009–2017).

Rade Uhlik (1899–1991) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied Germanistics at the University of Belgrade. He worked as a translator for Tanjug and as a custos at the National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
